result:
failure: result: The installed Pi extension reports that it carries the official Cua Windows driver; independent upstream verification remains blocked.
changed: none
checks: Read-only source inspection; no runtime, installation, or desktop checks run.
blockers: Web search and fetch failed: `exa provider requires EXA_API_KEY or apiKeys.exa in project or agent-directory pi-web-kit config.` Official Cua release and independent corroboration could not be checked.
questions: Whether “all capabilities” requires optional local OCR and whether the active Codex/Kimi host exposes every required tool remain unverified.
notes:
- Verified: The installed extension’s README says its MCP tool surface uses the official Cua Driver Rust 0.37.0 runtime; its Windows x64 `SOURCE.md` says it redistributes the upstream runtime “without modification.” This is the carrier’s claim, not independently verified upstream.
- Inference: Seeing `@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use` in Pi is expected for the integration, not evidence that the official driver is absent. The Windows x64 runtime package is present, but binary integrity and successful startup were not tested.
- Verified: T3 preview tools and desktop computer-use are separate capabilities in HolyAgent’s screen-agent contract; T3 preview availability depends on the host. The extension defaults to core tools, with additional groups discoverable or activatable. Optional perception is separate; the installed README lists Windows x64 but not ARM64 for Perception 0.2.1.
evidence:
Computer-use extension and official driver relationship is established from authoritative evidence: Installed `C:\Users\david.basile\.pi\agent\npm\node_modules\@amaster.ai\pi-computer-use\README.md` identifies the official 0.37.0 runtime; `C:\Users\david.basile\.pi\agent\npm\node_modules\@amaster.ai\pi-computer-use-cua-driver-win32-x64\SOURCE.md` identifies the release asset and SHA256. Both are carrier-supplied; upstream confirmation is blocked.
Recommended Windows path respects current integration contracts and names any unresolved requirement: Retain the installed Pi carrier and bundled Windows x64 runtime, rather than replacing it with a standalone driver; verify live tool discovery and Codex/Kimi access before claiming all capabilities. `packages/integrations/pi/dist/agents/reviewer-visual-screen.md` names both surfaces; the extension README documents `core`, `full`, and deferred tools.
sources: Installed extension 0.1.38 README and package metadata; installed Windows runtime package 0.1.4 metadata and `SOURCE.md`, claiming Cua 0.37.0; upstream release https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0 was inaccessible. Local artifacts have no checked publication dates.
recommendation: Keep bundled mode and existing screen-agent integration; use tool discovery or activation for non-core tools. Treat OCR installation and complete Codex/Kimi capability verification as unresolved, not as grounds for an unverified dependency replacement.
